TE3-F-01.hint: Find the angles in one turn \([0, 2\pi)\) with the unit circle. Then add \(2n\pi\) to each of them, or just \(n\pi\) for a tangent equation, where \(n\) is any integer.
slips: Adding \(2n\pi\) to a tangent solution. Tangent repeats every \(\pi\).
Giving one angle when sine or cosine takes the value at two angles in one turn.
Leaving out that \(n\) is any integer.

TE3-F-02.hint: Take the square root of both sides and keep both the positive and negative roots. Solve each equation with the unit circle.
slips: Finding the angles for only one of the two roots.
Listing the reference angle only, without placing it in each quadrant.

TE3-F-03.hint: Let \(u = k\theta\). As \(\theta\) goes from \(0\) to \(2\pi\), \(u\) goes from \(0\) to \(2k\pi\). Find every solution for \(u\) in that range, then divide each by \(k\).
slips: Solving for \(u\) only in \([0, 2\pi)\), which misses most of the solutions.
Dividing only the first solutions by \(k\) and forgetting to divide the added multiples of the period.
Forgetting to divide by \(k\) at the end.

TE3-A-01.hint: Move everything to one side, treat \(\sin\theta\) (or \(\cos\theta\)) as the variable, and factor. Set each factor equal to \(0\) and solve each equation on the unit circle.
slips: Dividing both sides by \(\sin\theta\) or \(\cos\theta\), which loses the solutions where it equals \(0\).
Rejecting \(\sin\theta = -1\) or \(\cos\theta = -1\) as impossible. Only values beyond \(-1\) and \(1\) are impossible.

parts.q: Find all solutions of \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\) (the general solution).
parts.a: In \([0, 2\pi)\) the solutions are \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\), \(\theta = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}\). Adding full periods (\(2\pi\)) gives all solutions: \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6} + 2n\pi \text{ or } \theta = \dfrac{5\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\), where \(n\) is any integer.
